items.name: GreenSight
items.headline: From zero coding to local research.
items.summary: In four weeks, middle schoolers went from no coding experience to using Python, data analysis, and machine learning to study where trees should be planted in the Bay Area.
items.outcome: They wrote a research paper identifying the best tree-planting locations and shared it with local city council members.
items.detail: We launched GreenSight to see what middle schoolers could do with data science and a real local problem. Students learned Python, worked with data, and used machine learning to investigate tree-planting locations in the Bay Area. Their work became a research paper that they shared with local city council members.
items.visualTitle: Where should we plant more trees?

items.name: Women in Afghanistan
items.headline: A way to receive income.
items.summary: We helped Afghan women set up Bitcoin and USDT wallets, working directly with Roya Mahboob, Natalie Brunell, and Speed Wallet.
items.outcome: This was part of a larger effort that has reached thousands of women in Afghanistan.
items.detail: Under the Taliban, women are shut out of banks, school, and most work. A digital wallet gives them a way to receive income for their families through online education work. We worked directly with Roya Mahboob, founder of the Digital Citizen Fund, Natalie Brunell, founder of Women in Bitcoin, and Speed Wallet to help women set up Bitcoin and USDT wallets.
items.visualTitle: Online work. A wallet. A way to get paid.

about.title: About us | Code4Cause
about.headline: It started with who was missing.
about.intro: At the hackathons we went to, there were almost no other girls in the room. We kept noticing it. In Summer 2025, we started Code4Cause.

chapters.label: 01 / The spark
chapters.title: Almost no other girls.
chapters.text: At the hackathons we went to, there were almost no other girls in the room. That was the starting point for Code4Cause: wanting more girls to have a place in computer science.

chapters.label: 02 / Our first program
chapters.title: Start with a real question.
chapters.text: We launched GreenSight to prove that middle schoolers could do real data science on a local problem. They started with zero coding experience. Over four weeks, they learned Python, data analysis, and machine learning, then wrote a research paper on the best places to plant trees in the Bay Area. They shared it with local city council members.

chapters.label: 03 / A clearer focus
chapters.title: Skills, confidence, and a path into CS.
chapters.text: After GreenSight, we refocused on girls in tech. We wanted to help girls build technical skills and confidence, and see a path into computer science careers. Code4Cause grew to 100+ chapters in 8+ countries.
chapters.more: That focus also led us to work with Roya Mahboob, Natalie Brunell, and Speed Wallet to help women in Afghanistan set up Bitcoin and USDT wallets. It was part of a larger effort that has reached thousands of women, giving them a way to receive income through online education work.

about.founderTitle: Three founders. One shared starting point.
about.founderIntro: We’re Aarya, Risha, and Sanvi. We founded Code4Cause together in Summer 2025.

mission.title: Our mission | Code4Cause
mission.headline: A path into computer science, for more girls.
mission.intro: Code4Cause focuses on getting girls into computer science and technology: building technical skills, confidence, and a path toward CS careers.
mission.body: We started by helping middle schoolers apply data science to a real problem in the Bay Area. Our focus grew to girls in tech, a network of chapters across countries, and work supporting women’s access to digital wallets in Afghanistan.
